sentences.text: Social worker Tom Okafor from Harbridge adult services visited Harold Pryce at his home, having been referred by Dr Bell.
Harold Pryce lives alone with his wife Sandra; his wife Sandra is currently at her sister's house for the day.
Harold and Sandra have been married for nine years; Sandra is his second wife, and his first wife Joan died in 2013.
Harold has a stick and a frame upstairs and reported a fall in the garden in the spring.
Harold has no falls since the spring incident.
Harold can wash himself but sits on a stool in the shower; he finds putting on socks difficult.
Harold can make a sandwich; his wife Sandra cooks his meals.
Harold disclosed that Sandra keeps his medication in her handbag and sometimes keeps his tablets back if he has annoyed her.
Harold reported he did not have his heart tablets for three days last week because Sandra kept them back.
Harold stated he has had his water tablets withheld by Sandra a few times.
Harold stated he does not want Sandra in trouble, but wants the abuse to stop and wants his tablets.
Harold stated he would be upset if Carol knew about the abuse, but agreed that Carol could be told.
Harold disclosed that his wife Sandra hits him with her walking stick when she gets cross.
Harold initially denied the bruises on his arms were caused by Sandra, stating he bruises easily with tablets, but later confirmed they were true.
Harold stated Sandra hits him on his arms when she gets cross.
Harold estimated the hitting happens once a week, or more if Sandra has had a bad day.
Harold disclosed that Sandra locks him in the bedroom when she goes out, claiming it is so he does not fall.
Harold stated Sandra locks him in the bedroom two or three times a week for the afternoon.
Harold noted there is no toilet upstairs while he is locked in the bedroom.
Harold stated that if he leaves the house, Sandra would take it, even though the house is in his name only.
Harold stated he feels safe at the time of the visit because Sandra is away at her sister's house.
Social worker Tom Okafor provided the number for the older people's advocacy service and instructed Harold to ring 999 if he is hurt or locked in.
Harold's daughter Carol lives in Kestwick, about two hours away, and calls him on Sundays.
Harold stated his pension goes into a joint account and Sandra does the bills; he has his own savings book at the post office.
Harold stated he has a mobile phone that Carol made him get.
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed raising a safeguarding concern with the team, arranging for Harold's tablets to be delivered in a blister pack from the chemist, and contacting a
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed contacting Harold's daughter Carol by Friday with Harold's permission.
Social worker Tom Okafor proposed referring Harold to an occupational therapist for assistance with socks and stairs.
Social worker Tom Okafor planned to return on Tuesday, the first of December, in the morning when Sandra is at her sister's.
